submitter: doc-subject vocabulary lockstep, 2026-08-09 (following through RFC_015's migration 340; owner-directed)
rationale:
WHAT IS WRONG. The doc-subject vocabulary has exactly two enforcement points by design — the two DB CHECK constraints (doc_plans_subject_type_check, doc_notes_subject_type_check) and one single-sourced Go slice, validDocSubjectTypes in platform/orchestration/actions/doc_subjects_common.go, consumed by both Go gates (docResolveSubject, shared by write_doc_plan/append_doc_note/load_doc_context, and the persist_diagnosis_note gate). Commit e1628f7df (RFC_015 decision records, owner-approved 2026-08-08) shipped migration 340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql, widening doc_notes' CHECK to accept subject_type='decision', and did not touch the Go slice. Its own file list confirms it: the migration and three platform files, none of them doc_subjects_common.go. That is a SPLIT CONTRACT — the DB accepts a value both Go gates reject — and it is the third instance of the same shape: migration 163 (+'experience') missed the persist_diagnosis_note gate; migration 184 (+'action') moved the DB CHECKs only, leaving its own seeded action docs unreachable through every doc action (bugs_closed/064); migration 270 (+'landmine') widened doc_notes alone and the DB accepted rows the Go gate rejected for two days, found only when landmine-verifier failed live at append_doc_note.

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT THIS TIME, AND WHY THAT MATTERS. Nothing failed live. TestValidDocSubjectTypes_LockstepWithMigrationCheck — written as the mechanical form of the dedup-index/Go-list lockstep lesson, and extended after 270 to watch BOTH constraints — caught it at committed HEAD, naming the drift, the two migrations and the union it expects. Verified against a clean `git archive HEAD` tree (b2371b4b5), not just the working tree, so the failure is HEAD's and not some session's WIP. This submission is the detector's own remedy being taken, which is the cheap half of the story; the expensive half was 270, where the same class was found by a live failure two days later.

WHAT THIS CHANGES. One value appended to validDocSubjectTypes, plus the history paragraph in the slice's binding comment that every prior addition has extended. It restores the invariant the test asserts: the Go vocabulary equals the UNION of the newest doc_plans CHECK (273_doc_subjects_component.sql) and the newest doc_notes CHECK (340). It is deliberately NOT an equality-with-either-alone: 'landmine' is already doc_notes-only, so the union gate is by construction slightly more permissive than either table, and 'decision' now joins it on exactly the same footing. See the risks block, where that asymmetry is stated plainly rather than left for a reviewer to find.

WHY IT IS NOT AN ARCHITECTURE-SCOPE CHANGE. Under the 2026-07-29 ruling, an addition to a shared vocabulary needs an RFC when it changes what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES. This changes no guarantee: it makes the Go gate agree with a constraint an owner-approved change already put in the database, and migration 340 records its own scope as 'additive and inert ... Nothing writes subject_type=decision until operators or agents type new decisions; no existing row or query changes meaning'. The seam here is not being widened — it is being un-split. The one consumer whose surface moves is the persist_diagnosis_note gate (see risks), and that widening is the point of single-sourcing the slice: 064's checklist item 3 rules that a diagnosis note about a subject should be persistable for every type in the vocabulary, decided deliberately rather than inherited silently.

plan.summary: Add "decision" to validDocSubjectTypes so the single-sourced Go vocabulary matches the DB CHECKs that migration 340 already widened, closing the split contract commit e1628f7df left behind and turning TestValidDocSubjectTypes_LockstepWithMigrationCheck green at HEAD. One-value change plus the binding comment's history entry; no behaviour changes for any existing row, and nothing dispatches subject_type='decision' through these actions until a document names it.

edits.rationale: The single source both Go gates read. Migration 340 widened doc_notes' CHECK to accept 'decision' and left this slice behind, so the DB accepts a value docResolveSubject and the persist_diagnosis_note gate both reject — the split contract this file exists to make impossible. The comment change is not decoration: this slice's history paragraph is the only place a reader learns WHICH table each asymmetric member belongs to, and 340 carries a landmine (the four staged decision rows are typed 'component', so queries must filter on `categories ? 'decision'`) that a reader arriving via this vocabulary would otherwise miss.

grounded_in: doc_subjects_common_test.go:167 at clean HEAD b2371b4b5: "split contract: validDocSubjectTypes = [action component experience experience-pattern landmine pipeline tool] but 273_doc_subjects_component.sql sets doc_plans to [tool pipeline experience action experience-pattern component] and 340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql sets doc_notes to [tool pipeline experience action experience-pattern landmine component decision] (union = [action component decision experience experience-pattern landmine pipeline tool]) — move both together (bugs_open/064; checklist: docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/experience_register/design/subject_type_addition.md)"

340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql, the constraint it installs: "ADD CONSTRAINT doc_notes_subject_type_check CHECK (subject_type = ANY (ARRAY['tool'::text, 'pipeline'::text, 'experience'::text, 'action'::text, 'experience-pattern'::text, 'landmine'::text, 'component'::text, 'decision'::text]));" — doc_notes only; the file never mentions doc_plans_subject_type_check.

340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql header: "SCOPE — additive and inert (2026-07-29 ruling: normal council gate, not an RFC of its own). Nothing writes subject_type='decision' until operators or agents type new decisions; no existing row or query changes meaning."

340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql header: "LANDMINE FOR READERS (same as 270's): filter on `categories ? 'decision'`, NEVER on subject_type='decision' — the four staged rows are typed 'component' and are real decisions."

git show --stat e1628f7df: the commit ships "docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/340_doc_notes_decision_subject_type.sql", "platform/orchestration/actions/decision_guard.go", "platform/orchestration/discovery_checks/check_decision_guards.go" and "platform/orchestration/actions/section_editor_actions.go" — doc_subjects_common.go is absent from the file list, which is the whole defect.

doc_subjects_common_test.go, the union contract stated in the test's own doc comment: "The two tables' vocabularies are allowed to diverge (doc_notes now accepts 'landmine', doc_plans does not — a landmine has no shared-contract shape to put in doc_plans), so validDocSubjectTypes is a UNION gate, slightly more permissive than either table's own CHECK alone: an out-of-place value passes this Go gate but is still caught by the target table's own CHECK at insert time, which is the same safe direction of imprecision the original test already accepted (a rejected write, never a silently wrong one)."

doc_subjects_common.go binding comment, the rule being restored: "It MUST agree with the DB CHECK constraints doc_plans_subject_type_check / doc_notes_subject_type_check — a value the DB accepts but a Go gate rejects, or vice versa, is a split contract; move both together."

doc_subjects_common.go, the prior instance of this exact class: "+'landmine' (migration 270, doc_notes ONLY — D10's LANDMINES.md sync. Found missing here 2026-07-31 by landmine-verifier's first live run: the DB accepted subject_type='landmine' on doc_notes for two days while this gate rejected it, the exact split bugs_closed/064 exists to prevent."

experience_register/design/subject_type_addition.md, item 3 (the deliberate policy this widening inherits): "Point-4 policy, decided deliberately (not silently inherited): diagnosis notes SHOULD be persistable for `action` and `experience-pattern` subjects (a diagnosis about a shared action or a pattern is exactly what the note trail is for)".
plan.risks:
THE ONE THING A REVIEWER SHOULD WEIGH — this widens BOTH Go gates, and one of them can now reach a value its target table will refuse. Because the slice is single-sourced, adding 'decision' widens docResolveSubject (write_doc_plan, append_doc_note, load_doc_context) AND the persist_diagnosis_note gate together; there is no way to widen one without the other, by design. doc_notes' DB CHECK accepts 'decision' after migration 340; doc_plans' CHECK (last set by 273) does NOT. So a write_doc_plan step configured with subject_type='decision' will now pass the Go gate and fail at the DB CHECK, where before it was refused earlier, in Go, with a clearer message. This is not a new hazard class: it is exactly the 'landmine' asymmetry the union contract already accepts and the test's own comment already licenses — 'an out-of-place value passes this Go gate but is still caught by the target table's own CHECK at insert time ... a rejected write, never a silently wrong one'. Stating it plainly rather than leaving it implied: the failure moves from a Go error to a Postgres constraint violation for one impossible-today configuration. If the council judges that unacceptable, the alternative is a per-table vocabulary (two slices, or a table-aware gate) — a strictly larger change that abandons the union contract 064 and 270 settled on, and one I would not smuggle in under a one-value fix.

WHAT IS NOT A RISK, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (a) No existing row changes meaning: this only ever ADDS an accepted value, and migration 340 records that nothing writes 'decision' yet. (b) No dispatch path reaches it today — the four staged RFC_015 decision rows are typed 'component' and are read by category, per 340's landmine, so the citation gate (decision_guard.go) and the guards check are untouched by this either way. (c) Order-of-deploy: the usual image-before-migration discipline does not bite here because the migration is already applied and it is the IMAGE that is behind — this change can only make the pod agree with the database, never the reverse, so there is no window it opens.

SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING FAILURE, DISCLOSED SO IT IS NOT READ AS MINE. `go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/` is not green before or after this change: TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry fails on two probe actions (test_only_bug136_create_work_item_without_configkeys and its _control) registered by create_work_item_config_contract_test.go, the bugfix-136 lane's file. Confirmed present at clean `git archive HEAD` (b2371b4b5) with this change absent, so it is HEAD's and belongs to that lane. Untouched here — it is another thread's work in flight, and the doc-subject vocabulary cannot affect the action registry.

VERIFICATION DONE. Named test red at clean HEAD, green after (`go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/ -run TestValidDocSubjectTypes_LockstepWithMigrationCheck -v`). TestDocSubjectGates_TableDriven passes, which is the real behavioural check: it drives every vocabulary member through BOTH Go gates, so 'decision' is proven accepted by docResolveSubject and by docSubjectGateReason, not merely present in a slice.
